title: Interear audiometric notch-depth disagreement does not improve cross-cohort tinnitus prediction in a prespecified model
abstract: We tested whether the absolute interear difference of 4-kHz notch depth adds predictive information for concurrent past-year tinnitus beyond conventional hearing summaries and notch indicators. NHANES2011–2012 supplied 3815 adults aged20–69 for model fitting; separately recruited2015–2016 supplied 4262 for frozen evaluation. Adding interear 4-kHz notch-depth disagreement changed cross-cohort Brier score from 0.124650 to 0.124877 (difference +0.000227; joint PSU-bootstrap95% interval -0.000439 to +0.001557). Source five-fold out-of-fold Brier improved slightly, but the registered cross-cohort criterion was not met. This is a specification-specific negative result, not equivalence or absence of physiological information. Both cycles were previously explored for other outcomes; no untouched or independent-study-program confirmation is claimed.
